title: 4 in 10 UK Teens Want More Work Experience at School
paragraphs: More than 40% of UK teenagers want more opportunities for work experience at school, with a similar percentage asking for more guidance on how to apply for jobs, a survey done for the BBC has found.
The online survey included 2,000 young people aged 13 to 18. They were asked for their thoughts on how school can better prepare them for employment and adult life.
Along with the 44% who said they would like more work experience opportunities in school, 43% also said they would like to learn how to manage their finances.

Forty-two percent said they want more guidance on how to apply for jobs, and 39% said they want to learn more about managing stress and mental health. Thirty-eight percent also said they'd like help improving their communication skills.

The survey was done as part of this year's Teen Summit event, which was hosted at Newcastle College — a secondary school — where students were given a chance to talk more about their thoughts and experiences.

Many students at the event talked about their worries about money. For example, Ella, whose second name was not shared, talked about how expensive it is to go to university, with students needing to pay around $13,000.
She added that even her entrance exam cost about $100. "I have to get a job because I can't afford all of this," she said.
Speaking about the event, Newcastle College student Elliot Smith said, "It was a really great experience hearing from people my own age about the challenges they're facing."
He also said he liked having the chance to share his own thoughts.
